planner.question: Can proof-system-independent circuit range avoidance deliver a single hard language within NP at an honestly charged cost?
planner.strategy: Construct least absent sparse truth-table prefixes for all bounded fan-in-two circuits.
planner.alternative: Audit superpolynomial budgets and compare uniform bounded program diagonalization.
planner.stop_rule: Reject fixed-exponent quantifier swaps and uncharged quantified oracles; no P versus NP promotion.

construct.claim: Sparse-prefix range avoidance yields fixed-exponent hard languages in P^Sigma2P with explicit bit cost and exact circuit size lower bounds.
construct.scope: All circuits with at most s ordered fan-in-two binary gates, free constants, n inputs.
construct.derivation: Count syntactic circuits; choose an absent prefix; use existential-word universal-circuit prefix completion and greedy search.
unresolved_steps: Place a single superpolynomial-hard language in NP or obtain a fixed NP-complete transfer.
candidate_tests: Compare ordered circuit enumeration with bit-parallel available-wire sets; exact least missing words.

alternative.claim: A growing circuit budget gives one language outside P/poly at charged superpolynomial construction cost, while uniform machine diagonalization gives a quasipolynomial-time language outside P.
alternative.scope: s=n^ceil(log2 n), explicit unary budgets, standard universal machine overhead.
alternative.derivation: Apply prefix avoidance at growing budget; separately complement bounded acceptance on padded self-codes.
unresolved_steps: NP membership of either constructed language; unrestricted SAT lower bound.
candidate_tests: Check exact counting inequality at small and larger symbolic budgets and prefix completion.
